speaker: (the boy)
text: A book for Master Shakespeare. My lord's house in Holborn. I am to leave it in a hand, and I am not to wait for an answer.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Open the latch. I have the corner of it, and I am not letting a boy try the stair.

speaker: (the boy)
text: My lord of Southampton, mistress. The slip is in the book. They said a proverb, and they did not tell me which.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am the hand. You have done the errand. There is nothing to carry back.

speaker: (the boy)
text: Then I am for Holborn, sir. The horse is at the street.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Alse, the door. I will take this up myself. I want to know what a lord's book weighs.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: It weighs more than the washing, mistress. I will take the latch. I will not take the book.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Read nothing yet. I will have the slip before we climb.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: The first line is plain enough. Lent, not given. The rest is a hand I do not keep a shop by.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Florio. Chi presta, perde: who lends, loses. And under it, prove the proverb false.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Then it is lent. It goes on your board. It does not go in the coffer with the letter, and it does not go home in a week's linen.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It will not. I will not write my name in a loan.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: The copper is on below for the Monday boiling. If the horn wants filling, it is twopence when the pot cools.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Fill it when it cools. Set the twopence by the dinner. This morning is the book.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Gib is on the third tread, sir. A folio and a cat will not take that turn together.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Move the cat, Alse. If it is lent, we are not spilling Monday's ink on my lord's proverb.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am opening it at the Knight. Theseus, if the book is the book I think. A duke riding home with a queen, and two young men at a window. I have till the bell for nine.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Are the two young men looking at one lady, sir?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: One lady, through a window. That is as far as the opening goes. I am not telling you a plot on a stair.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Nine, and then you eat. A folio is not a dinner. The loaf is yesterday's loaf. A penny, and a full thumb short of the notch.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: A penny. I heard it yesterday. I will be down when the bell goes.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I will move the cat. I will not dust a lord's leaves. Dust is a decision, and this is a loan.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Up, then. I have the weight of it, and that was all I wanted of Holborn. You may have the words.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will have them standing. If I sit, I will start a page, and this morning is his page, not mine.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Stand, then. And mind the clasps. Gib likes old leather, and this is not his.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I am for the copper, mistress. The latch is on the turn.
